subject.title: Feature request: first-class async result routing back to originating topic sessions

question: Should OpenClaw make async result routing a core Gateway registry, a plugin/SDK contract, or defer it until a concrete plugin API gap is proven?
rationale: The current source has the low-level wake and delivery pieces, but the requested route lifecycle, matching, storage, privacy, and action policy create new product/API surface that repository vision explicitly wants bounded before core expansion.

options.title: Plugin/API-first route contract
options.body: Define the minimal route/matcher/action interfaces and missing plugin seams first, then add core storage only for responsibilities plugins cannot safely own.

options.title: Core Gateway registry
options.body: Accept the feature as core-owned and design a SQLite-backed route store, matcher, ambiguity policy, and approval-safe action runner in Gateway.

options.title: Defer to local or plugin workflows
options.body: Keep the issue open as design backlog but continue using hooks, cron, targeted wake, and plugin-local ledgers until a concrete missing seam blocks implementation.

recommendation.title: Plugin/API-first route contract
recommendation.body: Define the minimal route/matcher/action interfaces and missing plugin seams first, then add core storage only for responsibilities plugins cannot safely own.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest current-history routing candidate and VISION/product-boundary evidence makes this primarily a product/API direction decision.
